newsitem.title: USA: Stocks soothed by tame inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks soothed by tame inflation data.

text.p: Stocks edged higher on Thursday as jitters about rising interest rates were soothed by another batch of economic data showing inflation was still in check.
At 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT), the Dow Jones industrial average was up 9.76 points at 7,938.08 after profit-taking ate into an early rise of 60 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 15-11 on volume of 281 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 3.55 points at 1,586.95.

"Volatility will continue until we get consistently low inflation that people truly believe and they see there is not going to be a major reacceleration in the economy," said Jennifer Moran, associate to the chief economist at Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.

The rally was spurred by a government report that the Consumer Price Index edged up 0.2 percent in July after rising 0.1 percent in June. The so-called "core" rate of inflation, which leaves out the often-erratic food and energy measures, also rose 0.2 percent.
The increase matched Wall Street expectations.

In another report Wednesday, the government said the Producer Price Index for July fell 0.1 percent, following an identical drop in June. Without the volatile food and energy components, wholesale prices also fell by 0.1 percent. It was the seventh straight month of declines in wholesale prices.

The inflation-sensitive bond market also rose, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond up nearly a full point, which lowered its yield to 6.56 percent from Wednesday's close of 6.63 percent. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The inflation numbers come just days before the Federal Reserve's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets next Tuesday.
"It's good news but we are getting a rather feeble and restrained response," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.
Moran said investors may be waiting for another month of good news on inflation, including confirmation that second-quarter gross domestic product growth was moderate.
"The market can go either way but ultimately it's the upside we are going," Jimmy Wilson, director of institutional trading at Anvil Institutional Services said.
"There is no reason for a massive correction -- there is too much money around and not enough places to put it other than in stocks," he said.
Micron Technology Inc. was again under pressure following Wednesday's downgrading by key analysts. Micron lost 7/16 at 42-3/16 in heavy trading.
Columbia/HCA was down 1-3/16 at 31-9/16. New York State's Comptroller filed a lawsuit against some of Columbia/HCA's officials.
